quick: One drop in the affected eye(s) once daily in the evening
Use only if benefit justifies risk; limited human data
Unknown if excreted in human milk; use with caution
No specific adjustment; use with caution in liver disease
Intraocular pressure; iris/periocular pigmentation; eyelash changes
summary: Bimatoprost is a synthetic prostaglandin (prostamide) analog eye drop used to lower elevated intraocular pressure in open-angle glaucoma and ocular hypertension. It increases aqueous humor outflow. Characteristic effects include conjunctival hyperemia, eyelash growth, and possibly permanent darkening of the iris and periocular skin. It is dosed once daily in the evening and should not be used more frequently.
indications: Reduction of elevated intraocular pressure in patients with open-angle glaucoma
Reduction of elevated intraocular pressure in patients with ocular hypertension

dosage.d: One drop in the affected eye(s) once daily in the evening
dosage.n: Do not exceed once-daily dosing - more frequent use reduces IOP-lowering effect

admin: Instill one drop into the conjunctival sac of the affected eye(s) in the evening
Do not administer more than once daily
If using more than one topical ophthalmic product, separate each by at least 5 minutes
Remove contact lenses before instillation and reinsert at least 15 minutes after (preservative benzalkonium chloride)
Avoid touching the dropper tip to the eye or any surface to prevent contamination
moa: Bimatoprost is a synthetic structural analog of prostaglandin (a prostamide analog). It lowers intraocular pressure by increasing the outflow of aqueous humor through both the trabecular meshwork and the uveoscleral routes, selectively mimicking the effects of naturally occurring prostamides.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to bimatoprost or any component of the formulation
relative: Aphakic or pseudophakic patients with torn posterior lens capsule, or those with risk factors for macular edema
Angle-closure, inflammatory, or neovascular glaucoma (limited experience)

preg: There are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women; postmarketing data show no increase in major birth defects or miscarriage. Animal studies showed abortion and adverse fetal effects only at oral doses many times the human ophthalmic exposure. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: It is not known whether bimatoprost is excreted in human milk. Because systemic exposure after ophthalmic use is very low, risk to the infant is likely minimal; use with caution and consider the benefit of breastfeeding.
renal: No specific dosage adjustment is required; systemic absorption after ophthalmic dosing is negligible.
hepatic: No specific dosage adjustment is required; abnormal liver function tests have been reported but systemic exposure is minimal.

moderate: Other topical prostaglandin analogs (paradoxical IOP elevation possible - avoid combining different prostaglandins)
minor: Other topical ophthalmic IOP-lowering drugs - separate instillation by at least 5 minutes
interactions.diagnostics: May be associated with abnormal liver function tests in a small percentage of patients

serious: Increased brown iris pigmentation (may be permanent)
rare: Hypersensitivity/allergic reaction including allergic dermatitis and eyelid edema
emergency: Severe eye pain with sudden vision loss
Signs of acute hypersensitivity reaction (eyelid swelling, dyspnea, asthma-like symptoms)

monitoring: Iris color and periocular/eyelid skin pigmentation
Signs of macular edema, especially in aphakic/pseudophakic patients
counsel: Use exactly once daily in the evening; using it more often will not work better and may work less well
Your iris (eye color) may gradually become more brown and this change can be permanent; the eyelids and lashes may also darken and lashes may grow longer/thicker
Remove contact lenses before use and wait at least 15 minutes before reinserting them
Do not let the dropper tip touch your eye or any surface to avoid infection
If you use other eye drops, wait at least 5 minutes between products; report any eye pain, redness, or vision changes
pk: IOP reduction begins approximately 4 hours after the first dose
Maximum IOP-lowering effect within approximately 8 to 12 hours
Plasma elimination half-life approximately 45 minutes (rapidly cleared systemically)
IOP-lowering maintained over 24 hours, supporting once-daily dosing
Store at 2-25 C (36-77 F); may be used until the printed expiration date after opening
pearls: Once-daily in the EVENING - more frequent dosing decreases the IOP-lowering effect of prostaglandin analogs
Iris and periocular skin darkening and eyelash growth are hallmark prostaglandin-analog effects; iris color change may be permanent
Use with caution in active intraocular inflammation and in aphakic/pseudophakic eyes at risk of macular edema
Do not combine two different prostaglandin analogs - may paradoxically raise IOP
missed: If you miss your evening dose, skip it and resume your normal schedule with the next evening dose. Do not use an extra drop to make up for a missed one.
overdose: No information is available on human overdose. Topical ocular overdose is unlikely to cause systemic toxicity given the very low systemic exposure. If accidental ingestion or overdose occurs, treatment is symptomatic and supportive.
